newsitem.title: USA: Korean firm to plead guilty to illegal contributions.
newsitem.headline: Korean firm to plead guilty to illegal contributions.

text.p: Haitai America Inc. will plead guilty to federal grand jury charges of illegal contributions in the 1992 election of Representative Jay Kim, a California Republican, a lawyer for Haitai said on Thursday.
"The company is expected to plead guilty pursuant to a negotiated agreement with the U.S. Attorney's office," said Brian Sun, a lawyer for Haitai.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Stephen Mansfield said on Tuesday the indictment charges Haitai with laundering $2,800 in illegal corporate contributions to the Kim campaign by using employee conduits and concealing the illegal contributions on the corporation's books and records.

Kim, the first Korean-American to serve in Congress, was alleged to have received illegal donations in his 1992 campaign in southern California's 41st congressional district, according to the U.S. attorney's office.
Haitai America, a unit of Haitai Group , a South Korean-based food company, faces a maximum fine of $400,000 if convicted on both counts.
Haitai America is the fifth South Korea-based company to plead guilty to charges of illegal contributions to the Kim campaign.
Hyundai Motor America, a unit of Hyundai Motor Service Co. Ltd., Korean Air Lines Co., Samsung America Inc. and Daewoo Corp. have previously pleaded guilty.
Criminal fines obtained against these four companies have totalled $1.2 million, the U.S. attorney's office said.
